features.feature: Settings → Plugins has tabs Installed (count), Discover, Marketplaces (count), opening on Discover when nothing is installed; Installed with none says "No plugins yet…"

Discover shows category chips and search, Featured then All plugins; each card names its marketplace and version with Install, Installed ✓, "Installed from another marketplace", "Needs a newer Echo" or "Can't be read"

Install opens a sheet first: name, version, marketplace, commit, "It will be able to" in Echo's words, a warning when Echo's own marketplace didn't list it (Cancel the default), why it can't when blocked; Cancel or the backdrop closes it
Installing adds the plugin enabled and its window part (buttons in its slots, panels, Settings section, ⌘K entries) loads; switching it off takes all of it out, on brings it back

An installed plugin's detail shows where it came from, the enable switch, Open its settings, Update to X or why not, Remove… (keep data / delete it), its own settings (switch, text, folder, secret with Forget) and what it can do
An update that asks for more shows the new lines on a sheet and waits for a yes

Marketplaces lists the built-in one (not removable) and added ones with how many plugins and when read, Read again, ⋯ hide / show its plugins, Remove; Add a marketplace (owner/repo, git address or folder, optional name)

A plugin hears only the Echo events it named (meeting soon, call start / end, recording start / stop, transcript ready, minutes written, thread synced, sources changed), with ids and titles, never the words
A plugin's Claude runs use only the user's AI profiles; its session skills reach only Echo's own sessions
`echoctl plugin list` gives installed, offered and marketplaces as JSON

A plugin may reach the address the user enters in a setting its manifest lists in `network.hosts_from`, and only that origin: the sheet says so, https works for any host, plain http only inside the user's own network, and an address that isn't allowed is refused where it is saved

A plugin's `ctx.http.fetch` with `save` keeps a download in its store byte for byte (a failed one leaves no file), and the window serves that audio or picture from `/plugin/<id>/store/…` and nothing else of the store
